recent_posts.title: Explore LLM word representations using similarity analysis (part 1)
recent_posts.summary: Representational Similarity Analysis (RSA) is introduced as a technique for comparing how different language models encode words internally. Rather than directly comparing embedding vectors between models like BERT and GPT-2 (which fails due to random initialization and different embedding spaces), RSA computes cosine similarities between word pairs within each model and then correlates those similarity patterns across models. The post walks through extracting embeddings from BERT-large and GPT-2-medium, demonstrating that direct correlation yields near-zero results, while RSA reveals shared semantic structure. Code is provided via GitHub/Google Colab. Part 2 will extend the analysis to transformer layers and category selectivity.

recent_posts.title: A knowledge graph mapping the structure of machine learning concepts
recent_posts.summary: A knowledge graph of machine learning concepts has been mapped out, revealing a hierarchy from foundational mathematics to state-of-the-art techniques. Key patterns include the central role of mathematics as a backbone and gradient descent as a pivotal concept enabling modern ML. The content is primarily a teaser pointing to a video, accompanied by a subscription pitch for deeper educational content.

recent_posts.title: The Power of Mathematical Modeling
recent_posts.summary: Mathematical modeling is explored through the lens of contagion, using the ILOVEYOU computer worm and zombie apocalypse scenarios as parallel examples. The post introduces compartmental models (SI, SIZR), explains how populations are grouped by state and connected by flow rates, and derives equations showing exponential growth and basic reproduction numbers. It then extends the framework from 'well-mixed' assumptions to networked worlds, showing how hub structure affects spread and control. The core message is that the same mathematical framework applies to viral code, biological disease, and ideas alike.

recent_posts.title: Explore Machine Learning as a Knowledge Graph
recent_posts.summary: A machine learning knowledge graph explorer has been built and made publicly available, mapping out ML concepts and their relationships. The interactive app, hosted on GitHub Pages, lets users visualize subfields, mathematical roots, central concepts, and trace prerequisites and dependents of specific topics like gradient descent. The source code is also available on GitHub.

recent_posts.title: Let’s Bring Jupyter Notebooks to Substack
recent_posts.summary: NotebookPress is a new tool that converts Jupyter Notebooks into Substack-ready posts in two clicks. It addresses four key pain points for technical writers: LaTeX rendering (with coloring and equation numbering), syntax-highlighted code snippets, Python-generated image outputs, and cross-platform compatibility. Code execution runs locally in the browser via Pyodide. The tool is currently in beta with a paid plan planned that will include LLM editing support, direct platform publishing automations, and an MCP integration.

recent_posts.title: Machine learning embeddings explained with Harry Potter examples
recent_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly deep dive into machine learning embeddings, using Harry Potter as a narrative framework. Covers why random numbers and one-hot encoding fail to capture word meaning, how Word2Vec learns dense vector representations from context, and how cosine similarity and vector arithmetic (king − man + woman = queen) work. Includes a practical demonstration: a Word2Vec model trained on the Harry Potter corpus, visualized with t-SNE, showing character clusters, semantic neighborhoods, and oddball detection. Concludes with real-world applications of embeddings in search engines, LLMs, image generators, and recommendation systems.

recent_posts.title: The Palindrome in 2026
recent_posts.summary: Tivadar Danka outlines his 2026 plans for The Palindrome newsletter: finishing his Machine Learning From Zero book with from-scratch algorithm implementations, creating more explainer videos, launching monthly live workshops for paid subscribers (starting with Mathematics of Machine Learning on March 7th), building a team of contributors inspired by distill.pub, and developing nb2wb—an open-source tool for converting Jupyter Notebooks to web publishing platforms. The newsletter has grown from 16,835 to 39,663 subscribers since May 2025.

recent_posts.title: Building and executing a space experiment on the ISS
recent_posts.summary: A researcher shares the complete journey of developing and executing a space experiment on the ISS, from grant proposal to data analysis. The project involved building an iOS app to study IMU sensor behavior in microgravity and reconstruct movement trajectories using inertial data. Key challenges included learning Swift/iOS development from scratch, navigating NASA and Apple Store approval processes, managing tight launch windows and delays, and coordinating with international space agencies. The experiment successfully collected data comparing sensor behavior on Earth versus microgravity, with preliminary trajectory reconstructions showing promising results.

recent_posts.title: Deriving the closed form formula for Fibonacci numbers
recent_posts.summary: The Fibonacci sequence has a closed-form formula expressed using the golden ratio and its conjugate, avoiding expensive recursive computation. Two mathematical approaches derive this formula: generating functions (treating sequences as power series coefficients) and eigenvalue decomposition of the Fibonacci matrix. Both methods reveal why the golden ratio appears in Fibonacci numbers and demonstrate how calculus, algebra, and combinatorics intersect to create powerful computational tools.

recent_posts.title: How did the Babylonians know √2 up to six digits?
recent_posts.summary: The Babylonians computed the square root of 2 to six-digit precision (99.9999% accuracy) around 1800-1600 BC, as evidenced by an ancient clay tablet. The article promises to explain their computational method but primarily serves as a teaser for a paid workshop on machine learning mathematics.

top_posts.title: The Camel Principle
top_posts.summary: The camel principle is a crucial mathematical technique that simplifies computation by adding or subtracting the same quantity without changing equality. Illustrated through both the quadratic equation and derivative calculations, this principle plays a vital role in methods like backpropagation in neural networks. Understanding these mathematical nuances allows for advancements in technology.

top_posts.title: Machine Learning From Zero is ready to go!
top_posts.summary: Machine Learning From Zero (mlfz) is an open-source project featuring a tensor library built from scratch and an interactive 100+ pages textbook on neural networks. The project aims to help readers understand neural networks by breaking them down and rebuilding them. Topics include computational graphs, backpropagation, and vectorization.

top_posts.title: The Roadmap of Mathematics for Machine Learning
top_posts.summary: Machine learning is built on three mathematical pillars: linear algebra, calculus, and probability theory. Linear algebra describes models through vectors, matrices, and transformations. Calculus enables model training through differentiation and gradient descent optimization. Probability theory provides the framework for making predictions under uncertainty, including concepts like expected value, entropy, and information theory. The guide covers essential topics from vector spaces and matrix operations to multivariable calculus and Bayes' theorem, providing a structured learning path from beginner to advanced understanding of neural networks.

top_posts.title: Ten lessons from 20 years of mathematics on learning and mastery
top_posts.summary: A mathematician with 20 years of experience shares ten key lessons about learning and mastery. The core insights include the importance of understanding fundamentals before breaking rules, learning through hands-on problem solving rather than passive consumption, and recognizing that there are no shortcuts to expertise. The author emphasizes taking things slow to build deep understanding, tackling complexity one step at a time, and finding the right perspective to solve problems. Other key points include the power of asking questions without shame, the primacy of hard work over talent, and the importance of forging your own path rather than blindly following others' advice.

top_posts.title: Coding on Paper
top_posts.summary: Coding on paper, despite seeming impractical without autocomplete or testing, serves as deliberate practice that strengthens fundamental programming skills. By restricting tools and making the process harder, developers build cognitive muscles for attention to detail, deliberate problem-solving, and independent thinking. This mirrors how athletes train with restrictions to improve performance, and how writing by hand helps form thoughts rather than just communicate them. The difficulty forces mastery of the process itself, not just the final product.
